name: Mouth is law

card.summary: A looksmaxxing framework holding that the mouth area (lips, smile, philtrum, teeth) weighs most heavily in facial attractiveness, pointing people toward lip, dental and perioral improvements.

quick.overview:
Mouth is law is a community saying that the mouth region carries unusual weight in how attractive a face looks. Proponents argue that lips, teeth, smile and the area around them are what viewers notice most.

The idea functions as a prioritisation rule: those who hold it put attention into lip shape, dental alignment and whitening, smile and perioral skin before other features. It circulates as forum shorthand rather than a formal theory, and users often post photos to argue about whether a given mouth fits it.
quick.how: Followers apply it by focusing on dental work, whitening, lip care or filler, smile practice and the lower face, and by judging photos with the mouth as the first feature.
quick.risks: Cosmetic dentistry and lip procedures carry their own procedure-specific risks and should be discussed with licensed professionals. The claim itself has not been tested in published studies.

lead: Mouth is law is a phrase used on looksmaxxing forums, including looksmax.org, asserting that the mouth is the dominant determinant of facial attractiveness. For people trying to improve their looks it directs effort at the mouth area: orthodontics and whitening, lip care or cosmetic lip procedures, and smile presentation.[1]
Discussion is largely informal photo debate in which users argue whether particular mouths illustrate or contradict the rule, with asymmetry cited as a factor that lowers a mouth's appeal.[1]
No study has tested a mouth-dominance rule as stated. Reference summaries of attractiveness research describe preferences for lip fullness that vary by culture and era.[2]

chain: Identify the mouth as a priority feature
Work on teeth, lips and smile
Mouth region reads as more attractive
angle.text: Believers use the idea to decide where to invest: dental alignment and whitening, lip shape and care, and smile. The weighting itself is a community claim.

paras: The phrase presents the mouth as the feature that decides how a face is judged. It is used both as an argument in rating discussions and as a guide for what to improve.

Followers describe prioritising dental alignment and whitening, lip care or filler, smile practice and the lower face, and judging photos with the mouth first. Cosmetic dentistry and lip procedures carry procedure-specific risks that professionals discuss with patients.

Reference summaries of attractiveness describe full lips as preferred by some men and in some traditions, while Chinese and Japanese texts favoured small lips, showing that the ideal has varied.[2] The same summaries cite classical descriptions of an attractive man with rosy lips and white teeth.[2]
Threads titled around the phrase mix photos with replies disputing whether the shown mouth is attractive. Posts are informal and opinion-based.[1]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the phrase appears in photo-rating threads where users argue about particular mouths.[1]

claims.claim: The mouth matters most for attractiveness
claims.believers: Proponents hold that lips, teeth and smile dominate first impressions and so deserve priority.[1]
claims.experts: Attractiveness summaries describe culturally variable lip preferences, and no published study has tested a mouth-dominance rule.[2]
